title: The Stability of Online Algorithms in Performative Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2602.24207v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The use of algorithmic predictions in decision-making leads to a feedback loop where the models we deploy actively influence the data distributions we see, and later use to retrain on. This dynamic was formalized by Perdomo et al. 2020 in their work on performative prediction. Our main result is an unconditional reduction showing that any no-regret algorithm deployed in performative settings converges to a (mixed) performatively stable equilibrium: a solution in which models actively shape data distributions in ways that their own predictions look optimal in hindsight. Prior to our work, all positive results in this area imposed strong restrictions on how models influenced distributions. By using a martingale argument and allowing randomization, we avoid any assumption on how populations respond to predictions and sidestep recent hardness results showing that deterministic stable models are in general PPAD-hard to compute. translated_title: 表演性预测中在线算法的稳定性
translated_abstract: 在决策中使用算法预测会引发一个反馈循环：我们所部署的模型会主动影响所观测到的数据分布，而这些数据随后又被用于重新训练。Perdomo 等人于 2020 年在其关于表演性预测（performative prediction）的工作中对这一动态进行了形式化刻画。我们的主要结果是一个无条件归约，表明部署在表演性环境中的任何无悔算法都会收敛到一个（混合）表演性稳定均衡：在这种解中，模型主动塑造数据分布，使得其自身的预测在事后看来是最优的。在本工作之前，该领域所有的正面结果都对模型如何影响分布施加了严格的限制。通过采用鞅论证并允许随机化，我们避免了对人群如何响应预测的任何假设，并规避了近期的困难性结果——这些结果表明确定性的稳定模型在一般情况下是 PPAD 难以计算的。最后，关于……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文证明部署在表演性预测环境中的任何无悔在线算法都会无条件收敛到（混合）表演性稳定均衡，且无需对人群如何响应预测做任何假设。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that any no-regret online algorithm deployed in performative prediction settings unconditionally converges to a (mixed) performatively stable equilibrium, without imposing any assumptions on how the population responds to predictions.
